name: Shillong
description: Capital city of Meghalaya and headquarters of East Khasi Hills district, known as the Scotland of the East for its rolling hills, pine forests, and colonial-era architecture. Serves as the main base for exploring waterfalls, caves, and living root bridges of the region.
facts: Capital and largest city of Meghalaya
Headquarters of East Khasi Hills district
Known for educational institutions and vibrant markets

name: Shillong Peak
description: Highest peak in Meghalaya at about 1,965 m, located south of Shillong city. Offers panoramic views of the city, surrounding hills, and distant plains. Sacred to the Khasi people as the abode of the deity U Lei Shillong; access controlled due to nearby Air Force installation.
facts: Sacred site for Khasi deity U Lei Shillong

name: Elephant Falls
description: Three-tiered waterfall on the outskirts of Shillong in Upper Shillong area. Locally known as Ka Kshaid Lai Pateng Khohsiew (three-step waterfall). Easily accessible with steps leading to viewpoints, popular for its cascading waters amid lush greenery.
facts: About 12 km from Shillong city centre
Named after a former elephant-shaped rock
Popular stop on the way to Sohra

name: Ward's Lake
description: Artificial lake and landscaped park in the heart of Shillong, also known as Pollock's Lake. Features a wooden bridge, boating facilities, and gardens; a popular recreational spot for locals and visitors amid colonial-era surroundings.
facts: Popular for boating and leisure walks

name: Don Bosco Centre for Indigenous Cultures
description: Major museum in Mawlai, Shillong, dedicated to the indigenous cultures of Northeast India. Displays ethnographic collections, traditional houses, textiles, and artefacts of Khasi, Garo, Jaintia and other tribes; one of the finest cultural museums in the region.
facts: Located in Mawlai area of Shillong

name: Sohra (Cherrapunji)
description: Town in East Khasi Hills famous as one of the wettest places on Earth. Gateway to numerous waterfalls, limestone caves, living root bridges, and viewpoints overlooking the Bangladesh plains. Known for heavy monsoon rainfall and lush landscapes.
facts: One of the wettest places on Earth
Base for exploring Sohra plateau attractions

name: Nohkalikai Falls
description: Tallest plunge waterfall in India, dropping about 340 m from the Sohra plateau edge into a turquoise pool. Located near Sohra, it is fed by monsoon rains and framed by steep forested cliffs; associated with a local Khasi legend of Ka Likai.
facts: Best viewed during monsoon for full flow

name: Nohsngithiang Falls (Seven Sisters Falls)
description: Segmented cliffside waterfall near Mawsmai village, plunging about 315 m in multiple streams over the plateau edge. Known as Seven Sisters Falls; offers dramatic views of the cascades and the plains below, especially during rains.
facts: Also known as Seven Sisters or Mawsmai Falls
Near Mawsmai village south of Sohra

name: Mawsmai Cave
description: Accessible limestone cave near Sohra with illuminated passages, stalactites and stalagmites. About 150 m long, it is one of the most visitor-friendly caves in Meghalaya, requiring some crawling in sections; part of the Sohra cave circuit.

name: Arwah Cave
description: Limestone cave near Sohra known for marine fossils embedded in its walls, including shells and fish remains. Accessible via a short trail; offers a glimpse of prehistoric geology amid the plateau landscape.

name: Mawlynnong Village
description: Village in East Khasi Hills near the Bangladesh border, widely recognised as Asia's cleanest village. Features community-managed cleanliness, bamboo pathways, a skywalk viewpoint, and a nearby living root bridge at Riwai; model of eco-tourism.
facts: Skywalk and Riwai root bridge nearby

name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge (Nongriat)
description: Unique two-tier living root bridge in Nongriat village, formed by guiding aerial roots of Ficus elastica trees over generations by the Khasi people. Requires a steep trek of about 3,500 steps from Tyrna; iconic example of indigenous bio-engineering in the subtropical forests.
facts: Trek from Tyrna village near Sohra

name: Laitlum Canyon
description: Dramatic canyon viewpoint about 25 km from Shillong, offering panoramic views of deep green valleys and cliffs. Known as the end of the hills; popular for photography and short visits, with access via Smit village.

name: Mawphlang Sacred Forest
description: Ancient sacred grove protected by Khasi traditional beliefs, located about 25 km from Shillong. Home to rare plants, old trees, and biodiversity; entry guided to preserve the spiritual and ecological site.
facts: Rich in medicinal plants and old trees

name: Mawsynram
description: Village in East Khasi Hills often recorded as one of the wettest places on Earth. Features caves like Mawjymbuin with a stalagmite resembling a Shiva lingam, and lush monsoon landscapes; quieter alternative to Sohra.
facts: One of the wettest places on Earth
